text:
Glory is like a circle in the water,
Which never ceaseth to enlarge itself
Till by broad spreading it disperse to nought.
plain: Glory spreads out like a ripple and then disappears. Nothing you win stays big on its own.

text:
Believe me, lords, my tender years can tell
Civil dissension is a viperous worm
That gnaws the bowels of the commonwealth.
plain: Infighting is a worm that eats a group from the inside.

text:
And here I prophesy: this brawl today,
Grown to this faction in the Temple Garden,
Shall send between the Red Rose and the White
A thousand souls to death and deadly night.
plain: One petty argument today turns into a war that kills thousands. Small grudges grow.

text: Defer no time, delays have dangerous ends;
plain: Delay is dangerous. Move now.

text:
Care is no cure, but rather corrosive,
For things that are not to be remedied.
plain: Worrying fixes nothing and eats at you. Don't brood over what can't be changed.

text:
Good Lord, what madness rules in brainsick men,
When for so slight and frivolous a cause
Such factious emulations shall arise!
plain: People tear things apart over trivial causes, and it is madness.
When the weak hold power it is bad, and when envy splits the people it is worse. That is where ruin starts.

text:
If we be English deer, be then in blood;
Not rascal-like, to fall down with a pinch,
But rather, moody-mad and desperate stags,
Turn on the bloody hounds with heads of steel
And make the cowards stand aloof at bay.
plain: If you are going to be hunted, turn on the hounds. Don't fall down at the first pinch.

text:
Sell every man his life as dear as mine,
And they shall find dear deer of us, my friends.
plain: If you have to go down, make them pay full price.

text:
There is no hope that ever I will stay
If the first hour I shrink and run away.
plain: If I run the first time I'm scared, I'll never stop running.

text:
If I today die not with Frenchmen’s rage,
Tomorrow I shall die with mickle age.
plain: If I don't die today, I die tomorrow anyway. One more day is a small thing to risk.

text:
Triumphant Death, smear’d with captivity,
Young Talbot’s valour makes me smile at thee.
plain: Death does not scare a man who has seen his son's courage. He can smile at it.

text:
Thou antic Death, which laugh’st us here to scorn,
Anon, from thy insulting tyranny,
Coupled in bonds of perpetuity,
Two Talbots, winged through the lither sky,
In thy despite shall scape mortality.
plain: Death mocks us now, but what we do can outlast it.

text: His fame lives in the world, his shame in you.
plain: Your reputation outlives you, and so does your shame.

text: Of all base passions, fear is most accursed.
plain: Of all the base feelings, fear is the worst.

text: A day will come when York shall claim his own;
plain: A day will come when I take what is mine.

text: Then, York, be still awhile till time do serve.
plain: Stay quiet and wait until the time is right.

text: Pride went before; Ambition follows him.
plain: Pride clears the road and ambition walks in behind it.

text:
My lord, ’tis but a base ignoble mind
That mounts no higher than a bird can soar.
plain: It is a small mind that never reaches higher than a bird can fly.

text:
Thus sometimes hath the brightest day a cloud,
And after summer evermore succeeds
Barren winter, with his wrathful nipping cold;
So cares and joys abound, as seasons fleet.
plain: Even the brightest day gets a cloud, and winter follows summer. Cares and joys come and go like seasons.

text:
Smooth runs the water where the brook is deep,
And in his simple show he harbours treason.
The fox barks not when he would steal the lamb.
plain: The quiet ones with the smooth surface may be the ones plotting. Watch the still water.

text:
A heart unspotted is not easily daunted.
The purest spring is not so free from mud
As I am clear from treason to my sovereign.
plain: A clean conscience is not easily scared. I am as free of guilt as the purest spring is of mud.

text:
Virtue is choked with foul ambition,
And charity chased hence by rancour’s hand;
plain: Ambition chokes virtue, and bitterness chases away kindness.
Pull weeds while they're shallow. Let them grow and they choke the garden.

text:
Thus are my blossoms blasted in the bud,
And caterpillars eat my leaves away;
But I will remedy this gear ere long,
Or sell my title for a glorious grave.
plain: My hopes were killed in the bud, but I'll fix it soon or die trying.

text:
Show me one scar charactered on thy skin;
Men’s flesh preserved so whole do seldom win.
plain: If you haven't been scarred, you haven't won anything.

text:
Now, York, or never, steel thy fearful thoughts,
And change misdoubt to resolution.
plain: Now or never. Steel your nerve and turn doubt into resolve.
